one_liner: Rust Windows .evtx parser and evtx_dump CLI; 8.8x faster than libyal's C evtxexport on one thread (same run).
what_it_does: Parses Windows XML EventLog (.evtx) files, the chunked binary-XML format behind Security, System and Application logs, and renders every record as XML or JSON. It ships as the `evtx` crate (EvtxParser::from_path / from_buffer / from_read_seek, then records(), records_json() or per-chunk byte renderers), the evtx_dump command-line tool, Python bindings (pyevtx-rs, PyPI `evtx`) and a WebAssembly viewer. It replaces libevtx's evtxexport for bulk conversion, but it is not a drop-in: the CLI flags differ, the XML text is not checked to match evtxexport's, and there is no C API.
how_it_is_fast: Since 0.12.2 (June 2026) each binary-XML template is compiled once per file into a constant text buffer and a short list of fill-in instructions (copy literal range, format value N, run a nested template), shared across worker threads through a content-keyed cache. Each record then formats its raw value bytes straight into the output with fused SIMD UTF-16-to-UTF-8 escaping (SSE2 or NEON), with no per-record tree or value enum. libevtx, by contrast, builds a libfwevt XML document for every record and then serialises it twice (a size pass, then a copy pass). Chunks are rendered in parallel on a rayon pipeline into bumpalo arenas and written with one write_all per chunk; release builds add thin LTO, codegen-units 1, optional jemalloc and PGO.
when_to_use: Bulk conversion of large .evtx files (tens of MB to GB) to JSON Lines or XML for SIEM ingestion, DFIR timelines or DuckDB/jq analysis, where libevtx's evtxexport takes seconds per 30 MB file.
You want JSON directly: evtxexport writes only text or XML, while evtx renders JSON from the same compiled templates without an XML-to-JSON step.
Multi-core machines processing one big log: chunks parse in parallel (README: 20.7 ms at 8 threads vs 71.6 ms on one thread for the 30 MB sample), with chunk order preserved by the pipeline.
Rust, Python (pyevtx-rs wheel) or browser (WASM viewer) codebases that need an embeddable parser with no C toolchain.
Damaged or dirty logs: it keeps reading past the header's chunk count and has basic record and chunk recovery.
when_not_to_use: You need output that matches evtxexport or Windows Event Viewer byte for byte: the XML layout differs (evtx_dump prints 'Record N' lines unless told not to), and no equivalence check against libevtx exists.
Logs that use CDATA or EVTHandle nodes, which README lists as unimplemented.

Forensic work that needs every typed value preserved: open issue #289 reports that BoolType fields holding values other than 0 or 1 (for example a 320060673 NTFS attribute mask) are silently turned into true, and the maintainer reply did not settle a fix.
C or C++ projects that want a linkable library: evtx has no C ABI; libevtx and its Python bindings remain the C option.
Pipelines that rely on chunk CRC checks: evtx skips checksum validation by default (--validate-checksums is opt-in), while libevtx always computes both chunk CRC-32 values and flags corrupt chunks.

integration.form: crate (also evtx_dump binary, PyPI wheel via pyevtx-rs, WASM build)
integration.dependencies: bitflags, crc32fast, byteorder, thiserror, log, winstructs, ahash, serde, serde_json, sonic-rs, zmij, jiff, bumpalo, in-repo utf16-simd, an ANSI codec crate (encoding in 0.12.3, encoding_rs on master); optional rayon (default 'multithreading'), clap/anyhow/simplelog/dialoguer/indoc/tempfile (default 'evtx_dump'), goblin and glob ('wevt_templates'), tikv-jemallocator or rpmalloc ('fast-alloc')
integration.min_toolchain: Rust edition 2024, so Rust 1.85 or newer; no rust-version is declared in Cargo.toml or on crates.io
integration.platforms: any Rust target with std; SIMD UTF-16 fast path on x86-64 (SSE2, runtime detected) and aarch64 (NEON), scalar elsewhere; release binaries for 64-bit Windows, macOS and Linux
integration.thread_safety: Parallelism is internal: ParserSettings::num_threads (0 = rayon's thread count) runs chunks on a bounded rayon pipeline that yields chunks in order; the iterators borrow the parser mutably, so one parser serves one consumer. Sharing a parser across threads is not documented.
integration.drop_in_for_baseline: partial — replaces evtxexport for converting .evtx to XML (and adds JSON), but with a different CLI, a different XML layout, no C API, and CDATA/EVTHandle nodes unimplemented

gotchas: Benchmark harness: the README's headline 34x (1 thread) and 118x (8 threads) pair a June 2026 evtx run with a libevtx figure (2.439 s) carried over unchanged from the January 2026 run on another kernel; only the January run is same-run (275.9 ms vs 2.439 s, 8.8x). The README figures come from the PGO plus fast-alloc (jemalloc) binary, but scripts/bench_all_parsers.sh builds a plain 'cargo build --release' and libevtx at an unpinned HEAD (configure.ac is now version 20261009) with autoconf default flags, so the committed script does not reproduce either side of the table. build_pgo.sh trains on every file in samples/, which includes the benchmark input security_big_sample.evtx (README puts PGO at 2-5%).

Work is not identical: libevtx computes two CRC-32 checksums per chunk on every run, evtx skips checksum validation unless --validate-checksums is passed. On the 2.4 s baseline this is small, but it is extra work only the C side does.

README and docs/compiled-templates.html say the crate is 100% safe Rust 'including the SIMD UTF-16 conversion'; the evtx crate root does carry #![forbid(unsafe_code)], but the in-repo utf16-simd dependency that does the SIMD escaping uses raw pointers, Vec::set_len on MaybeUninit buffers and SSE2/NEON intrinsics (42 'unsafe' occurrences in simd.rs), and sonic-rs is also unsafe internally.

README still warns that multithreaded evtx_dump may print records out of order; the 0.12 chunk pipeline reorders completed chunks (BTreeMap keyed by sequence) before yielding, so that note looks stale. The compiled-templates write-up calls the release 'v0.13' while it shipped as 0.12.2.
pick_this_over_siblings_when: No other EVTX parser is catalogued; among the format-parser siblings (mail-parser for MIME, PDFOxide for PDF text, YARA-X for rule scanning) pick evtx whenever the input is a Windows .evtx log, and treat its speedup as the same kind of design win as mail-parser's rather than a Rust-versus-C result.
verified_claims_summary: On a 12-core Ryzen 3900X (Arch Linux, hyperfine, 2 warmups, 5 runs), converting the 30 MB, 62,000-record security_big_sample.evtx to XML on /dev/null took 275.9 ms with evtx on one thread and 79.5 ms on 24 threads, against 2.439 s for libevtx's evtxexport -f xml in the same January 2026 run (8.8x and 31x). The current README's 71.6 ms (1 thread) and 20.7 ms (8 threads) come from the June 2026 PGO and jemalloc build and are compared with that January libevtx figure, so 34x and 118x are cross-run ratios. Compiler versions are not stated for either side.
status_note: Actively maintained (last commit 2026-10-07, 0.12.3 released 2026-09-22, about 311,000 crates.io downloads), dual MIT/Apache-2.0, with an unreleased breaking change on master that swaps the ANSI codec type to encoding_rs; copyable as a crate or prebuilt binary.
